issues.description: The template's Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature includes an extra boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) while the problem statement and the solution expect addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. This mismatch is structural and will confuse students about the required method signature and cause incompatibility with the intended solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template to match the specification and solution: change the method signature in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement the expected behavior. Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and solution to document and use the two-parameter signature consistently.

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with a different signature (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) than specified in the problem UML and implemented in the solution (addGuestStudents(int)). This parameter mismatch creates confusion: the problem statement and solution expect a single int parameter for adding guest students, while the template requires an extra boolean that is not mentioned anywhere else, making it unclear which method students should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the UML and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } Remove the extra boolean parameter 'validateInput' from the template method so students can directly implement the intended API.
